# Aindle

> A private, read-only AI work board for a desk — or a jailbroken Kindle Oasis 1 lock screen.

Aindle is self-hosted. The public website is an introduction plus mock demos. The hub stays on your LAN or Tailscale. It shows quotas, 24h/7d token spend, and in-progress / awaiting-confirmation / background tasks. It does not track productivity, approve work on the Kindle, or display prompts, replies, paths, or secrets.

## Start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Octo-o-o-o/aindle.git
cd aindle
npm install
npm run hub
```

Needs Git and Node.js 20+ (22+ on Windows for Cursor / Kiro / ZCode sqlite). The package is not on npm. First `npm run hub` compiles `@aindle/core` if needed. No database or extra Aindle service.

Then open:

- Board: http://127.0.0.1:8787/monitor.html
- Lock-screen HTML: http://127.0.0.1:8787/eink.html?page=local
- Lock-screen PNG: http://127.0.0.1:8787/dash.png?page=local (needs Chrome, Chromium, Edge, or Brave)

Same commands on macOS and Windows (PowerShell or cmd), from this clone. Do not type a bare `aindle`.

The hub seeds mock data on host `mbp` so the screen is not empty. `AINDLE_SEED_MOCK=0` (PowerShell: `$env:AINDLE_SEED_MOCK='0'`) turns the sample off. Live machines (local bin, not a global npm package):

```bash
npx aindle init --local
# edit ./config/registry.yaml — uncomment only tools you already use
npx aindle agent --loop 60
```

`init` stamps this computer's name (never `mbp`), so the sample stays until you disable it. Every tool in the starter file is commented.

On a Kindle Oasis or Scribe, open the Experimental Browser and type `https://aindle.octoooo.com/oasis` or `https://aindle.octoooo.com/scribe` to see the mock board on that device.

Optional Kindle Oasis 1 lock screen: copy `kindle/oasis1/` to `/mnt/us/aindle`, copy `hub.env.example` to `hub.env`, set `HUB` to the LAN URL on port `8787` (never `127.0.0.1` on the device), start from KUAL, then lock.

## What it is not

Not a public SaaS. Not a TokenTracker / OctoMonitor fork. Not a billing invoice. Not a scoreboard. Unlocking the Kindle returns the stock reader.
